explanation_en: Milk that has been dried into powder form. Contains milk proteins and lactose.
A dairy product made from the liquid left after churning butter.
Butter that has been simmered to remove milk solids and water; still a dairy-derived product.
The clear part of an egg, separate from the yolk.
A protein most commonly derived from egg white, used as a binder or foaming agent.
An enzyme derived from egg white, sometimes used as a natural preservative in cheese.
Oil pressed from peanuts. Highly refined peanut oil is sometimes tolerated by peanut-allergic individuals, but should still be avoided without medical advice.
A paste made from ground peanuts.
A tree nut, often used whole, sliced, or ground into flour.
A tree nut commonly used whole or as a paste/butter.
A tree nut common in chocolate spreads and confectionery.
A tree nut, often used chopped or as an oil.
A concentrated protein extracted from soybeans.
A fermented condiment made from soybeans; many varieties also contain wheat.
Flour milled from wheat grain. Also a source of gluten.
The concentrated protein (gluten) extracted from wheat flour.
A coarse flour milled from durum wheat, common in pasta.
A condiment made from fermented fish, common in Southeast Asian cooking.
A concentrated flavouring made from anchovies.
Gelatin derived from fish skin/bones, used as a gelling agent.
A flavouring made from dried, ground shrimp.
A flavouring derived from crab, sometimes used in imitation seafood.
Oil pressed from sesame seeds.
A paste made from ground sesame seeds.
A preservative that inhibits the growth of mould, yeast and some bacteria.
A preservative widely used to prevent mould and yeast growth in food.
A preservative and colour-fixative used mainly in cured meats; consumption is regulated due to nitrosamine formation risk when overheated.
A natural acid used to add tartness and control acidity; also acts as a preservative.
Vitamin C, used both as a nutrient and to prevent browning/oxidation.
An antioxidant closely related to vitamin C, used to preserve colour and freshness.
A common thickening and stabilising agent produced by fermenting sugar with bacteria.
A thickener/stabiliser extracted from red seaweed.
An artificial low-calorie sweetener. Not suitable for people with phenylketonuria (PKU).
An artificial low-calorie sweetener made from sugar.
A synthetic orange-yellow food colouring; some studies link azo dyes to hyperactivity in sensitive children.
A synthetic red food colouring; some studies link azo dyes to hyperactivity in sensitive children.
A mildly sweet carbohydrate filler made from starch. Not an allergen itself, but can be derived from wheat or corn.
A thickening agent derived from guar beans.
A preservative commonly used in bread to inhibit mould growth.
